pageCache.text:
Embrace every journey
Our boundless opportunities give pupils the space to discover who they are and the confidence to run with it.
A Welcome from our Head
“Welcome to Crosfields, and thank you for taking the time to visit our website. What excites me most about our school is not that our pupils follow a particular path. It’s that they don’t.
I often remind pupils not to place limits on themselves. My role, and our role as a school, is to create an environment where every young person has the confidence to aim high, the character to embrace the joys and challenges life will bring, and the freedom to define their own version of success.”
Mrs Caroline Townshend, Head
Read more from our Head
Dive in
A Snapshot of Life at Crosfields
Explore our latest news, key facts and next steps as you learn more about life at Crosfields, and see how our community thrives through curiosity, connection and confidence.
Crosfields Celebrates Outstanding GCSE Results
At a glance
A glimpse into the environment, opportunities and support our pupils enjoy every day. Find out more
Recognised for excellence.
“ Acres of games pitches, all-weather Astro and a big, beautiful sports hall with fitness suite and dance studio. Hockey, lacrosse, netball and rowing all going strong. Notable former Crosfields pupils are mainly in the sporting world, especially rowers and cricketers. ”
We chose Crosfields for its intimate setting that catered to our son’s specific needs. The nurturing environment allowed Tommy to blossom, boosting his confidence and embracing his authentic self. ”
“ Many schools say they offer a ‘whole-school approach’ but here it’s really true. One school. One community. Teetering on the brink of glory. ”
“ I love it here, which is why I have stayed at Crosfields School since Reception. The teachers are supportive. ”
“ Pupils develop resilience and perseverance, encouraged and supported by teachers and coaches. ”
“ Leaders have fostered an inclusive educational environment where pupil welfare is paramount, pupils respond positively to this provision and appear happy and confident. ”
“ I was particularly drawn to how the school provides equal opportunities for all and emphasises this. ”
“ Reflecting on my cherished moments at Crosfields, our surfing and yoga trip to Biarritz was more than just activities; it was an opportunity for us to unwind, bond, and create lifelong memories with friends. ”
“ What a great school Crosfields is now. Not only the amazing new classrooms but the staff and pupils, we were very impressed by it all. ”

GCSE Results
Outstanding Results in 2025
Crosfields School is proud to celebrate the exceptional achievements of its second cohort of GCSE pupils. In 2025, 39 Year 11 students sat their exams, and their results reflect not only academic excellence but also the school’s evolving legacy of ambition, resilience, and community spirit.
Headline Achievements
“We are proud of each and every pupil who sat exams this year. The hard work and dedication were impressive to see; over a number of years and in particular over the exam period, and I am delighted for the pupils and staff that this has paid off in a truly outstanding set of results.”
Deputy Head Academic (Seniors)
Outstanding top-grade performance included:
History – 75%
Computing – 72%
Biology & Chemistry – 63%
Physics – 56%
Business & Psychology – 53%
Pupil Destinations
All pupils achieved the grades required for their chosen Sixth Form or college pathway. Pupils progress to an impressive range of destinations including state and independent Sixth Forms, further education colleges and grammar schools, with several awarded academic scholarships.
Celebrating Success
Staff and pupils have shown exceptional dedication throughout the year, resulting in a truly outstanding set of results. Crosfields also celebrates individual achievements, including national recognition such as the ISA Whitbread Memorial Prize.
“These results mark a significant step forward for Crosfields and reflect not only the hard work and resilience of our pupils but also the exceptional teaching and support provided by our staff. Crosfields is proving itself to be a superb choice for secondary education, combining academic excellence with the breadth of opportunity that develops confident, well-rounded young people.”
Mrs Caroline Townshend, Head

pageCache.pageTitle: Creative & Performing Arts | Co-educational School Reading | Crosfields School
pageCache.text:
Creative & Performing Arts
Crosfields’ Creative Arts are a vibrant, inclusive hub where pupils from Nursery to Year 11 develop confidence, imagination, and a lifelong love of performance. Music and Drama pulse through school life, offering every child the chance to shine on stage, behind the scenes, or through innovative digital creation. With a rich curriculum, state of the art facilities, global cultural experiences, and a dynamic blend of traditional and cutting edge technologies, the arts at Crosfields nurture talent, celebrate individuality, and inspire creative expression at every stage of a pupil’s journey.
Music at Crosfields
Music is woven through the life of Crosfields, inspiring our pupils and filling the school with creativity and joy. Every child from Nursery to Year 9 enjoys a dedicated hour of music each week, building core skills, exploring global musical traditions, and experiencing the thrill of performance. GCSE musicians take this further with three hours of specialist teaching focused on compositionset works learning, theory, and performance. More than 200 pupils also take individual lessons each week, enriching their musical journey beyond the classroom.
Throughout the year, pupils take part in a rich calendar of concerts and events, including seasonal performances, Scholars’ and GCSE showcases, piano recitals, House Music, and major school celebrations. Whether performing as soloists, in ensembles, or as part of one of our six choirs, every pupil has the opportunity to shine. Our ensembles cater to a wide range of interests, from orchestra to guitar, harp, musical theatre, digital music groups, and more. Younger pupils explore instruments such as ocarinas, recorders, xylophones, ukuleles, and keyboards, laying strong foundations for future musicianship.
In Seniors, pupils engage with industry standard platforms such as Cubase, composing and recording like professional musicians. They also experiment with AI supported tools to create revision aids, short films, and digital compositions, ensuring they are well equipped for the modern creative landscape.
Drama at Crosfields
Drama at Crosfields provides a lively, ambitious environment where pupils learn to communicate with confidence and collaborate creatively. Guided by our ethos of “teach to the top and scaffold up,” every child, from our youngest performers to our exam groups, is encouraged to stretch their imagination and develop expressive, articulate performance skills.
Our professional-standard theatre gives pupils a space to grow as performers, directors, choreographers, designers, and technicians. As pupils progress through the school, they take on increasing responsibility for lighting, sound, set design, costumes, and backstage roles, gaining authentic hands-on experience across all areas of production. Technology enhances Drama lessons at every stage. Pupils explore virtual set, lighting, and costume design, create AI-generated podcasts to support revision, and even develop AI-assisted costume concepts linked to exam responses. This fusion of traditional performance craft and innovative digital practice deepens understanding and expands creative possibilities.
Drama at Crosfields also champions global perspectives. Pupils study influential texts from writers such as Malorie Blackman, Wole Soyinka, and Bertolt Brecht, and they participate in specialist workshops ranging from physical theatre to scare acting. These experiences broaden their knowledge of world theatre and help foster a sense of belonging, empathy, and cultural appreciation.

pageCache.pageTitle: Key Stage 3 | Senior School Reading | Crosfields School
pageCache.text:
Key Stage 3
Key Stage 3 at Crosfields offers a broad and inspiring curriculum that nurtures curiosity while building strong academic foundations. Pupils study a wide range of subjects, including English, Maths, Science and Languages, alongside Arts, Humanities, PE, Design Technology and Computing. This broad approach ensures every pupil experiences a balanced education that encourages exploration, creativity and confidence as they progress through Seniors.
Academic challenge and support
Our teaching approach is simple: teach to the top and scaffold up. Pupils are continually stretched and supported, helping them develop independence, critical thinking and resilience. Through high expectations and tailored guidance, pupils gain the skills and mindset needed for the demands of GCSEs and future learning. This approach ensures every child feels challenged and capable, growing in confidence as they take on increasingly sophisticated academic tasks.
Preparing for GCSE choices
In Year 9, pupils begin making their GCSE choices from a wide selection of subjects, including creative arts, humanities, languages, sciences and specialist pathways. This breadth enables them to shape a programme of study aligned with their interests and aspirations. Additional opportunities, such as opting for separate sciences, offer further challenge for those seeking to extend their academic journey. This thoughtful guidance helps each pupil make informed decisions as they prepare for the next stage of their education.
Beyond the Classroom
Learning at Crosfields extends far beyond traditional lessons. Through the Senior Enrichment Programme, pupils take part in enterprise initiatives, digital literacy awards, Model United Nations and the Higher Project Qualification. They can also explore sports, performing arts, STEM clubs and begin the Duke of Edinburgh Award from Year 9. XFP explores transferable skills, careers, oracy, revision techniques and entrepreneurship. These opportunities help pupils develop confidence, teamwork and leadership while discovering new passions and strengthening the skills they’ll draw on throughout their school journey.
Our academic ethos
We place high value on effort, rigour and resilience, encouraging pupils to think independently and approach learning with curiosity. Lessons are designed to challenge and inspire, helping pupils grow into confident, enquiring learners. Throughout Key Stage 3, our academic ethos ensures pupils are well prepared not only for GCSEs but for the wider demands of a rapidly changing world. They leave Crosfields equipped with strong foundations and the mindset needed to thrive.
Learning takes place in exceptional facilities within the award winning Aspire building, designed to inspire and support every stage of development. With extensive enrichment opportunities and a forward-thinking approach to teaching, pupils grow in ambition, confidence and curiosity, preparing them for the challenges and opportunities of life beyond school.
Innovative learning environment
Pupils benefit from an innovative and technology rich environment, including 1-2-1 Microsoft Surface devices and the use of VR and augmented reality in science. They have access to specialist facilities such as science labs, design workshops, performing arts studios and digital suites. These resources support dynamic, hands-on learning, helping pupils develop practical skills and confidence in new and emerging technologies.
A strong sense of belonging
Small class sizes and excellent pastoral care help every pupil feel known, valued and supported. Form tutors, House Leads, and Heads of Year build close, meaningful relationships with pupils, ensuring they have consistent guidance throughout their Senior School journey. House activities, sports and collaborative projects create a strong sense of community, strengthening friendships and encouraging pupils to contribute positively to school life. This supportive environment helps every child feel part of a thriving, inclusive community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Key Stage 4 | Senior School Berkshire | Crosfields School
pageCache.text:
Key Stage 4
Crosfields School’s Key Stage 4 offers an ambitious and personalised pathway for pupils in Years 10 and 11, combining core GCSEs with a broad range of options and enrichment opportunities. With around 120 pupils, the programme is designed to balance academic stretch with tailored support, helping every learner grow in confidence. Digital literacy, including the ethical use of AI, is embedded throughout the curriculum to prepare pupils for the future.
Academic excellence
Pupils follow a strong core of English Language & Literature, Mathematics and Science, complemented by diverse GCSE choices such as Art & Design, Astronomy, Drama, Computer Science, Business, Economics and Design Technology. For those seeking additional challenge, an Additional Mathematics enrichment course is offered. Every pupil benefits from expert teaching, targeted support and structured guidance aimed at helping them achieve their personal academic goals and thrive throughout their GCSE years.
Beyond the classroom
Learning at Crosfields extends far beyond exams. Pupils take part in enrichment experiences including creative writing competitions, theatre trips, coding challenges and national maths contests, encouraging them to explore new interests and build confidence. Opportunities such as Silver DofE and global expeditions to Malaysia and Thailand further enrich school life. These activities foster curiosity, leadership and resilience, helping pupils find their strengths and develop skills that last well beyond their time at school.
Wellbeing and outstanding facilities
Wellbeing is central to the Crosfields experience. Pupils benefit from workshops, stress-management strategies and a supportive environment that helps them navigate the demands of their GCSE years. Learning takes place in the award-winning Aspire building, bright, modern and designed to inspire, with specialist spaces that encourage hands-on experimentation and creative thinking. This combination of pastoral care and exceptional facilities ensures pupils feel confident, capable and ready for life beyond school.
GCSE Options
GCSE Core Subjects Include:
English Language - AQA
Our English Language curriculum is designed to inspire and motivate pupils. We aim to challenge pupils appropriately while ensuring that the assessments and reading materials are accessible to all.
We will help pupils of all abilities develop key skills in reading, understanding, and analysing a variety of texts from the 19th, 20th, and 21st Centuries. Additionally, they will learn to write clearly and accurately, using a range of vocabulary, devices and sentence structures.
There are two main exams, both equally important and untiered, that connect reading and writing. The texts they read will serve as inspiration for their writing tasks, guiding them through the exams. Each paper has a unique focus to encourage engaging teaching and learning.
Assessment:
Paper 1 – Explorations in Creative Reading and Writing
Written exam – 1 hour 45 minutes/50% of GCSE (80 marks)
Paper 2 – Writers’ Viewpoints and Perspectives
Written exam – 1 hour 45 minutes/50% of GCSE (80 marks)
Enrichment Activities:
Workshop opportunities
Creative writing opportunities in the co-curricular programme
English Literature - AQA
We have carefully chosen our English Literature curriculum to captivate and challenge all pupils, no matter their ability. Our goal is to create lessons that are creative and engaging, helping every pupil reach their full potential. The range of texts we have selected includes both familiar classics and exciting new works that are sure to capture pupils’ imaginations.
Pupils will be assessed in two exams, which are both closed-book and untiered. Questions take a variety of formats: some based on specific extracts; some without extracts but a choice of two tasks, and one section where they will be introduced to brand new content on which to practise their literature analysis and evaluation skills (as found in the unseen poetry section within paper 2).
Our curriculum is focused on helping pupils develop the key skills needed to study English literature, regardless of the genre. In addition to preparing pupils for future English Literature courses at AS and A-level, we hope that this subject offers a rich foundation in a wide variety of literature that will leave a lasting impact.
Assessment:
Paper 1 – Shakespeare and the 19th Century novel
Written exam – 1 hour 45 minutes/40% of GCSE (64 marks)
Paper 2 – Modern texts and poetry
Written exam – 2 hours 15 minutes/60% of GCSE (96 marks)
All English Literature examinations are closed text.
Section C: Unseen Poetry (32 marks)
Enrichment Activities:
Theatre and Workshop opportunities
Book club opportunities in the co-curricular programme
Mathematics - Edexcel
Mathematics is an exciting, creative and rigorous discipline that is at its most rewarding when it presents a challenge! As well as being a pursuit in its own right, mathematics underpins almost all areas of modern-day life. Pupils will be encouraged to appreciate the importance of sound mathematical understanding, whether that be as a gateway to further study in mathematics, engineering, the sciences or computing, or as the basis of good decision-making in their everyday lives.
The key aims and objectives of the Mathematics GCSE course are to enable pupils to:

Higher Tier

Assessment:
The Higher tier will be graded from 4 to 9. The Foundation tier will be graded from 1 to 5. During Year 10 we will decide if each pupil will sit the Higher or Foundation tier. Those very able students will also have the opportunity to sit an Additional Mathematics qualification.
The course is assessed completely via exams: three equally weighted exam papers, each 1 hour and 30 minutes long (one non-calculator, two calculator) all sat in the Summer Term of Year 11.

Intermediate and Senior Maths Challenge
Maths ‘clinics’ for supporting students
Maths-themed hobbies
Science AQA (Combined)
Science is a set of ideas about the material world. This course includes all the parts of good science whether it be investigating, observing, experimenting or testing out ideas and thinking about them. The way scientific ideas flow through the course will support pupils in building a deep understanding of science. This will involve talking, reading and writing about science plus the actual doing, as well as representing science in its many forms both mathematically and visually through models. GCSE science encourages the development of knowledge and = understanding in science through opportunities for working scientifically.
Syllabus:
Alongside the skills outlined in the course aims, all pupils will continue to nurture a curiosity of the world around them. Pupils will be encouraged to consider the power and limitations of science and the impact on our wider global community. Science will be taught in the 3 recognised areas of science Biology, Chemistry and Physics.
Pupils begin their GCSE Science course at the start of Year 9 with all pupils following 2 topics from each sciences giving a good foundation for either GCSE science course. As part of the options process, pupils may decide if they will sit a GCSE in each area of science or a combined Science course worth two GCSEs. This decision will be made with advice based our experience of the pupils’ scientific ability.
Assessment:
Combined (Trilogy) Science GCSE 6 x 1 hour 15-minute exams – 2 for each science. Resulting in 2 combined GCSE grades.
Enrichment Activities:
Trips to GCSE Science Live
Take it Further tasks guide independent learning
Weekly clinic devised to support learning
GCSE Options include:
Additional Mathematics - OCR
The OCR Level 3 Free Standing Mathematics qualification (FSMQ) in Additional Mathematics gives pupils an introduction to the mathematics studied in AS and A Level modules.
Taught alongside GCSE Mathematics in Years 10 and 11, it is designed as an enrichment programme for pupils who will be very high achieving at GCSE (9-1). This Level 3 course will give pupils an excellent grounding for any future mathematical studies.
Syllabus:
The FSMQ builds on the skills, knowledge and understanding acquired during the GCSE (9–1) course. It consists of four main ‘pure’ mathematics topics, each of which contains an ‘applied’ dimension, and two numerical topics, all underpinned by an algebra section.
Enumeration
Coordinate Geometry
Pythagoras and Trigonometry
Calculus
Numerical Methods
Exponentials and Logarithms
Assessment:
The examination consists of one 2-hour paper, taken alongside GCSE Mathematics in Year 11.
The assessment has a gradient of difficulty and consists of a mix of short and long answer questions, graded on the scale A, B, C, D, E where A is the highest.
Art, Craft and Design - AQA
The GCSE specification covered at Crosfields allows pupils to develop their skills in a range of media, selecting areas of strength and developing these in preparation for entry onto a number of A Levels within the arts (fine art, photography, textiles etc).
Pupils are able to specialise in fine art (drawing and painting), ceramics, textiles or printmaking. Alternatively, they can continue to use a range of media, keeping their options open. All pupils must include an element of drawing.
The course is ‘teacher led’ to begin with, but as Year 10 goes on, pupils have more choice in their work, and the teacher assumes a more supporting role. By allowing the pupils the independence to make their own decisions, they are well prepared for A Level.
Assessment:
The GCSE is assessed through the completion of two units:
Component 1 – 2 x Coursework projects. September Year 10—December Year 11. 60% of GCSE grade. Two projects, that can be made using a range of media (clay, painting, drawing etc). Each project should include drawings, photographs, artist studies, experiments and a final piece.
Component 2 – 1 x Exam project. January Year 11—May Year 11. 40% of GCSE grade.
Pupils are given an exam paper in January with multiple questions (E.G. “Portraiture”, “The Every day”, “Dreams and nightmares”, “Black and White”). Pupils pick one question and create a final project under this title—the final piece is completed in May over two days (10 hours).
Enrichment Activities:
Visits to local galleries
Visiting specialists
Business - Edexcel, IGCSE
Pupils will explore real business issues and investigate how businesses work. They will analyse the activities which happen behind the closed doors of businesses; managing money, advertising, and employment are all covered. The course gives pupils the opportunity to develop communication skills, numeracy in the real world, evaluative skills, organisation and teamwork. This is a great basis for those looking to work in the corporate world, or own their own business.

Assessment:
The course has two exams at the end of Year 11, both 90 minutes in duration.

Computer Science - Edexcel
The GCSE Computer Science courses has been designed to reflect the importance of computation in the modern world today and how it will do so in the future. Pupils will be able to understand and apply the fundamental principles and concepts of Computer Science and analyse problems in computational terms through practical experience such as designing, writing and debugging programs.
Pupils are encouraged to think creatively, innovatively, analytically, logically and critically to understand the impact of digital technology on the individual and wider society.

Design and Technology, Three-Dimensional Design - AQA
The GCSE Three-Dimensional Design course at Crosfields allows pupils to develop their intellectual, creative, and practical skills through the design, prototyping, and modelling of functional and aesthetic products, objects, and environments.
Areas of Study:
Pupils will work in one or more areas of three-dimensional design throughout the course, including:
Architectural design, Sculpture, Ceramics, Product Design, Jewellery and body adornment, Interior design, Environmental, landscape, and garden design, Exhibition design, 3D digital design, Designs for theatre, film, and television
Pupils may also explore overlapping areas and combine different specialisms.
Knowledge and Understanding:
Pupils will explore how sources of inspiration influence the development of ideas in three-dimensional design, considering:
Constructional considerations and imaginative interpretation

The GCSE is assessed through two components:
Component 1 – Coursework (60%)
Component 2 – Exam Project (40%)
Drama - Edexcel
This qualification encourages creativity and has a focus on practical work. This allows pupils to develop an understanding and enjoyment of Drama, developing group and individual skills and studying ways to communicate ideas and feelings to an audience.

Seniors Co-Curricular & Enrichment
Inspiring curiosity, confidence and character beyond the classroom
At Crosfields, learning does not end when lessons finish. Our Senior Co‑Curricular and Enrichment Programme is a defining feature of school life, broad, ambitious, and purposefully designed to extend every pupil’s experience far beyond the curriculum. Running from 16:30–17:30 each day, the programme gives pupils the space to explore interests, discover new passions, and challenge themselves in a supportive and vibrant environment.
We believe that education flourishes when pupils are given opportunities to grow creatively, intellectually, socially and physically. The Senior Programme provides these opportunities in abundance, combining teacher‑led clubs, specialist coaching, enrichment pathways and nationally recognised awards.
A rich and varied co‑curricular offer
Many of our activities are delivered by talented and passionate members of the Crosfields teaching team and are included in school fees. These clubs focus on academic enrichment, physical development, creativity, and personal growth. Current options include:
These activities allow pupils to push boundaries, connect with peers, and develop a sense of independence and confidence that is carried back into their academic work.
Running and Fitness
STEM: hands‑on science and engineering investigations
Strength and Conditioning: guided physical training
Netball
Jewellery Making

pageCache.text:
Seniors Sport
At Crosfields, pupils in Years 7 to 11 benefit from a vibrant and varied sports programme designed to inspire participation, develop talent, and encourage a lifelong enjoyment of physical activity.
Our Senior pupils enjoy access to a broad selection of major sports, including football, hockey, rugby, netball and cricket, alongside multisport opportunities such as basketball, badminton, swimming, tennis and forest school activities. This flexible offer allows pupils to pursue their interests while fulfilling curriculum expectations, ensuring every young person can find a sport they feel confident and excited to engage with.
Weekly fixtures form an important part of school life, giving pupils the opportunity to represent Crosfields with pride. We compete in a full calendar of matches across all core sports, and our teams regularly take part in Berkshire Schools events and national ISA/IAPS and knockout tournaments. We are committed to maintaining a strong sporting reputation, striving for excellence while ensuring that every pupil experiences the enjoyment and values that sport brings.
Families are warmly welcomed to lend their support from the sidelines, helping to create the vibrant sense of community that defines our match days. This shared enthusiasm not only celebrates our pupils’ achievements but also strengthens the spirit that runs through Crosfields sport.
Our PE & Games programme offers an exceptional, well‑structured curriculum that inspires pupils to excel. Through dynamic lessons, dedicated training sessions and a wide range of competitive opportunities, pupils develop teamwork, discipline and a lifelong appreciation for physical wellbeing. The programme nurtures confidence, resilience and leadership, while also fostering a strong sense of pride and belonging within our school community.
Beyond the core programme, pupils have the opportunity to further develop their skills through specialist pathways in athletics, tennis and a wide range of additional sports. This broad and inclusive offering ensures that every Senior pupil enjoys a rich and varied sporting journey, helping them build fitness, confidence and valuable life skills that stay with them long after they leave the pitch.
Swimming continues to play an important role in our Senior School programme. Several development squads run before school, led by specialist swimming staff who support pupils in refining technique, building stamina and progressing at their own pace. Alongside this, our Social Swim sessions offer a relaxed and enjoyable opportunity for pupils to swim lengths under the guidance of a qualified member of staff, without the pressure of competition.
We also take part in swimming galas throughout the year against other schools, giving pupils regular chances to represent the school in a supportive and spirited environment. For those who wish to pursue swimming further, we enter a range of national competitions, providing exciting opportunities for pupils to challenge themselves at a higher level.

pageCache.text:
Working at Crosfields
Crosfields is a vibrant, future focused day school where staff are inspired to deliver exceptional education within a supportive and fulfilling environment. With more than 700 pupils and a culture built on kindness and ambition, we take pride in creating a community where both children and colleagues can thrive. Our modern, forward-thinking approach encourages pupils to learn, grow, and actively shape the future of our school. As we look ahead to our 70th anniversary and the launch of our Sixth Form in 2027, it’s an exciting time to join us.
We’re always interested to hear from people who are passionate about children’s education or working within Support or Operations at Crosfields. Please send your enquiries by email to recruitment@crosfields.com.
Staff Benefits at Crosfields:
School Fee Remissions
Generous Pension Scheme

Professional Development

Our commitment to excellence
At Crosfields, educational excellence is at the heart of everything we do. Our dedicated staff work collaboratively to create dynamic learning experiences supported by modern facilities and innovative teaching practices. We remain committed to staying ahead of educational trends so that both pupils and educators can reach their full potential. Whether through creative teaching, inspiring classroom environments, or enriched co-curricular opportunities, our focus is always on delivering the highest quality of education.
A supportive community
Joining Crosfields means becoming part of a warm, inclusive, and collaborative community. Our staff value teamwork and shared success, supporting one another to create the best possible educational environment. We celebrate a culture of openness and encouragement, welcoming staff ideas and ensuring everyone feels connected to the school’s direction and values. This sense of community extends to wider engagement, with opportunities for involvement in outreach, activities, and events that strengthen ties across the school and beyond.
Opportunities for growth
We believe that professional growth is essential for staff fulfilment and long-term success. At Crosfields, colleagues have access to ongoing training, mentorship programmes, and regular opportunities to develop their skills and explore leadership pathways. Our commitment to nurturing talent ensures that ambitious and passionate educators can progress confidently in their careers. Whether you’re looking to specialise, innovate, or step into a leadership role, we are committed to helping every member of staff reach their full potential.
Our Values
Everything we do at Crosfields is rooted in our strong values. Kindness, commitment, ambition, growth, and integrity shape the way we work, teach, and collaborate. These values underpin our culture, guide our decisions, and help us create an environment where pupils and staff feel supported, respected, and empowered. When you join Crosfields, you become part of a community that strives each day to live these values and contribute positively to the life of the school.
Innovative Teaching
Crosfields is dedicated to embracing progressive and engaging teaching methods. From technology enhanced learning to project based approaches and interactive classroom experiences, our educators have the tools and freedom to inspire curiosity and creativity. By staying informed about evolving educational trends, we ensure our pupils receive a rich and relevant learning experience, while our teachers benefit from a culture that encourages innovation and professional exploration.
Staff Wellbeing and Benefits
We take the wellbeing of our staff seriously and offer a comprehensive package of benefits designed to support health, happiness, and work–life balance. Staff enjoy daily complimentary lunches and refreshments during term time, including hot beverages, snacks, and fruit, with breakfast available at a subsidised rate.
Our wellbeing offering includes allocated access to the school’s swimming pool and strength and conditioning suite, up to 40% off Nuffield Health membership, and a dedicated employee wellbeing platform through the UNUM app. This platform provides a 24/7 remote GP, mental health support, physiotherapy, second medical opinions, financial and legal guidance, lifestyle content, and access to an online lifestyle coach and personal trainer.
A dynamic Staff Wellbeing Team also organises events and initiatives throughout the year, ranging from BBQs for staff and families to running clubs with a coach, book club, Friday sport sessions, Walking Wednesdays, and our much loved Secret Buddies scheme.
Additional benefits include fee remission for staff children (minimum 25% pro rata for parttime roles), participation in our contributory salary sacrifice pension scheme, income protection, death in service cover, and staff discounts at Stevensons, Ultimate Activity holiday camps, B&Q, and Nuffield Health. INSET childcare support is also available.
All staff benefits are noncontractual and may be amended or withdrawn at any time.
Safeguarding and Recruitment
Crosfields is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. All positions require thorough pre-employment checks, including references, online checks, and an enhanced DBS check.
We comply with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act (ROA) 1974, noting that our posts are exempt from the Act, and we follow all right to work requirements under the Asylum and Immigration Act 1996. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to present identification, proof of address, right to work documentation, and original qualification certificates.

Key Stage 2 Curriculum
Key Stage 2 Curriculum
At Crosfields, Key Stage 2 is a time of discovery, ambition and growing independence. Our curriculum is designed to spark a lifelong passion for learning, empowering every child to aim high and achieve more. Through a broad and dynamic programme taught by expert subject specialists, pupils are inspired to think deeply, question boldly and embrace every opportunity ahead.
Innovative learning for a changing world
Innovation sits at the heart of our approach. From Year 3 onwards, pupils build strong digital literacy skills through hands-on experiences in Computing, Science and the Creative Arts. They learn programming, explore digital design, take part in interactive science experiments and engage with emerging technologies such as augmented and virtual reality.
Alongside classroom learning, pupils in Years 4–6 use personal devices to enhance and extend their studies, giving them the confidence to navigate technology with purpose. Co-curricular digital opportunities, from coding clubs to robotics challenges, further nurture future-ready skills.
A diverse, inclusive and empowering curriculum
With diversity recognised as one of our School’s greatest strengths, our curriculum reflects a rich mix of cultures, perspectives and learning experiences. Pupils encounter global literature, multicultural stories and creative work from a wide range of voices. This inclusive approach ensures that every child sees themselves reflected in what they learn, while also broadening their understanding of the world around them.
Specialist teachers support different learning styles and abilities, adapting lessons to stretch, challenge and support every pupil. Our “teach to the top” philosophy ensures that ambition is encouraged, celebrated and fully scaffolded.
Opportunities that broaden horizons
Opportunity shapes daily life at Crosfields. Pupils enjoy a wealth of enrichment options including STEM projects, robotics, cookery, photography, enterprise activities and performance. National competitions, from maths challenges and general knowledge quizzes to writing and STEM awards, offer further chances to shine, with our pupils consistently reaching national finals.
Our calendar of day trips, workshops, visiting speakers and residentials brings learning vividly to life and helps pupils connect classroom study with real-world experiences. All of these opportunities are included within our fees.
Building independence and readiness for Seniors
As pupils progress into Years 5 and 6, they move between specialist classrooms, mirroring the structure of Senior School and nurturing independence, organisation and confidence. Combined with clear communication between school and families, termly reports, parents’ evenings and book looks, every child is supported to thrive.
Curriculum
Years 3 and 4
Pupils in Years 3 and 4 are taught by their form teacher for the majority of their lessons. These years are crucial for building a strong foundation in academic subjects whilst developing the skills pupils need across the curriculum. We nurture individual aptitudes, foster a thirst for learning and ensure personalised provision benefits every pupil. This phase of the pupils’ exciting Junior journey secures their sense of identity and belonging, fully preparing them for the path ahead.
Our curriculum is enhanced by trips and an annual residential, which are all included within our fees.
Here’s a glimpse of what residentials our Year 3 and Year 4 pupils have to look forward to:
Years 5 and 6
Year 5 brings new experiences with specialist teaching for all subjects. Pupils move from room to room and are taught by specialist teachers in specialist teaching rooms: such as our Junior science lab. Time with form teachers at the beginning and end of each day is part of our nurturing framework that supports pupils as they build on their personal organisation, self-discipline and motivation. This model ensures that pupils are adequately prepared for the pattern of study that they will experience in Seniors. In Year 6, our pupils are ready to take on the challenges of more leadership responsibilities.
Our many enrichment opportunities, trips and an annual residential, included within our fees, unlock potential and the key 21st century skills such as teamwork, problem-solving, collaboration and critical thinking.

Seniors
Crosfields Seniors is a vibrant, academically ambitious community where pupils are encouraged to aim high and supported to achieve their personal best. Our teaching philosophy centres on “teach to the top and scaffold up”, ensuring every pupil is both challenged and guided as they grow in confidence and capability. This commitment reflects our wider dedication to innovation, diversity and opportunity, three pillars that define a Crosfields education.
A broad and enriching education
Opportunity is embedded in every aspect of school life. Our enriching and varied programme includes sessions on sleep and breathwork, the £10 entrepreneurship challenge, podcasting, and insights into creative and cultural careers, all designed to broaden horizons and build confidence.
Learning extends far beyond the classroom. Pupils enjoy trips ranging from STEM visits to Williams F1 to eco-sustainability expeditions in destinations such as Malaysia and Thailand, experiences that nurture curiosity and develop global awareness. In keeping with our forward-looking culture, we equip pupils with future-ready skills through modern learning environments and an agile curriculum that adapts to individual strengths and interests.
Character, independence and community
Every pupil is encouraged to discover their individuality and express it with confidence, a defining feature of our boundless and embracing school community. Through the Duke of Edinburgh’s Award in Year 9, pupils develop resilience, leadership and teamwork as they take part in expeditions and volunteering.
Across Seniors, pupils contribute to the wider community by supporting local charities and helping younger pupils with reading, Maths and clubs. Our personalised approach allows us to tailor pathways, whether adjusting timetables for talented athletes, offering additional GCSEs such as Dance, Mandarin, Italian or Astronomy, or providing bespoke pastoral and academic support. Pupils also benefit from time with Woody, our much-loved therapy dog.
An inspiring place to learn
Crosfields Seniors is based in Aspire, our award-winning, architect-designed building filled with natural light and purposefully created to support motivation, collaboration and focus.
Here, pupils follow the ASPIRE Learning Profile, developing resilience, independence and the mindset needed to embrace real-world challenges. This reflects our expert, research-informed approach to learning and wellbeing, which helps pupils understand themselves as learners and thrive within a rapidly changing world.
We are committed to supporting, encouraging and challenging every pupil throughout their Senior years. Our specialist teachers provide high-quality academic guidance, helping pupils excel across subjects and preparing them for demanding future pathways. As pupils progress, they benefit from an expanding curriculum that allows them to choose subjects that reflect their interests, passions and long-term goals.
A community dedicated to growth
Crosfields pupils are known, valued and supported. We work in partnership with families to help every child grow into a confident, capable young person ready to make meaningful contributions to society. Our exceptional facilities and expansive grounds provide the space, inspiration and opportunity pupils need to explore their interests and pursue their ambitions. This is a community where belonging matters, and where pupils feel free to be themselves.
Looking ahead: Our new Sixth Form
Opening in 2027, the Crosfields Sixth Form marks an exciting new chapter, building on our values of ambition, integrity, kindness and growth. With dedicated facilities in the newly refurbished Chestnuts building, pupils will benefit from inspiring spaces for independent study, collaboration and specialist teaching.
The Sixth Form will offer a broad range of A Levels and BTEC qualifications, strong pastoral care and a rich co-curricular programme, ensuring every pupil is supported as they prepare for life beyond school. It will be a vibrant, ambitious community where pupils are encouraged to lead, explore and grow into the very best version of themselves.

Onward Journey
At Crosfields, every pupil is supported as they take the next steps in their educational journey. We are proud that 100% of pupils have achieved the grades required for their first-choice future school. With over 35 destination schools across just two Year 11 cohorts, it’s clear that there is no single pathway; instead, we prioritise the right individual route for every learner. Our all-through approach ensures guidance begins early and continues throughout their time with us, with structured support, leadership development and tailored preparation for the exciting opportunities ahead.
Careers Education at Crosfields
We are passionate about equipping pupils with the knowledge, confidence and skills to navigate their future careers. Careers education is embedded from Juniors to Seniors, ensuring pupils explore a wide range of possibilities. Guest speakers, workplace visits and curriculum-linked discussions create meaningful insight into the world of work. From Year 1 to Year 11, careers themes are woven into the PSHE curriculum, helping pupils develop aspirations early. By the time they reach Seniors, pupils benefit from weekly careers sessions, themed awareness weeks and opportunities to connect learning with real-world pathways.
Careers in the Juniors
Our careers programme begins in Juniors, where curiosity is encouraged through engaging, age-appropriate experiences. Professionals from a variety of industries visit the school to share their stories, offering pupils an exciting first look at the world of work. Carefully planned educational trips to local workplaces broaden their understanding further, inspiring children to imagine what their own futures might hold. These early encounters spark ambition and help pupils recognise that their interests, talents and questions all play a role in shaping who they may become.
Careers in Seniors
In Seniors, careers guidance becomes increasingly tailored and practical. Weekly “Focus on Careers” sessions help pupils explore how curriculum subjects relate to future opportunities, while national awareness events such as Green Careers Week deepen their understanding of emerging industries. As they progress through each year group, pupils build a clearer picture of their strengths, motivations and ambitions. This structured, age-appropriate programme ensures that when pupils reach their GCSE years, they feel confident making decisions about subject choices, pathways and future goals.

Our careers journey builds progressively:
Celebrating Success
Our pupils continue to excel beyond Crosfields. Former School Captain, Febe Fisher, progressed to her chosen Sixth Form and became Head of College after only one year, a testament to the strong leadership development at our school. Many pupils secure scholarships in academics, arts and sport, and others successfully gain places at local Grammar Schools.
We are proud of standout achievements such as Ameya Dhanjal, who won the ISA Whitbread Memorial Prize in 2024 for exceptional academic outcomes and service to her community. These successes highlight the values, ambition and resilience nurtured at Crosfields.

pageCache.pageTitle: Seniors School Day | Senior School Reading | Crosfields School
pageCache.text:
Seniors School Day
The school day typically begins with morning registration, although some pupils choose to start earlier by joining our supervised Breakfast Club from 07:30. After meeting with their tutor, pupils take part in a rotating schedule of activities, which may include tutor time, a Collect (assembly), singing practice, or a House Meet. Lessons begin at 09:00.
Most lessons last one hour, with the occasional half-hour session. Pupils enjoy two one-hour lessons before break at 11:00.
Learning resumes at 11:30 and continues until lunchtime. Lunch is served in The Hatch from 13:00, with Years 10 and 11 remaining in lessons until 13:30 due to their staggered timetable.
The academic or sporting curriculum restarts at 14:00 (14:30 for Years 10 and 11), followed by two further one-hour lessons. The day ends at 16:00 for pupils in Years 7–9, while older pupils finish at 16:30.
After school, pupils may stay on to join Prep (homework) Club in the library or take part in a wide range of extracurricular activities. Clubs run until 17:30, and the library remains open for independent study until 18:00.

House System & Pupil Leadership
At Crosfields, we believe that leadership opportunities enrich every aspect of school life and play a transformative role in a child’s personal development. From their earliest years with us, pupils are encouraged to discover their strengths, build their confidence and contribute positively to their community. Leadership at Crosfields is not limited to formal positions; it is embedded in daily experiences that nurture responsibility, curiosity and teamwork. Many of our pupils tell us that stepping into a leadership role becomes a defining moment in their school journey, a chance to challenge themselves, develop their voice and feel genuinely valued within the school community.
Growing confident, capable leaders
Our wide range of leadership roles allows pupils to develop essential skills including public speaking, problem-solving, communication, organisation and creative thinking. We regularly see even the most reserved children flourish as they take on new responsibilities and discover their strengths.
Leadership roles give pupils purpose, build confidence, and support positive wellbeing. Opportunities include:

Our House system is central to daily life at Crosfields, creating community, healthy competition and a strong sense of belonging.
Pre-Prep
In Pre-Prep, children join one of four Houses: Maple, Ash, Willow or Beech. These Houses create a fun, supportive environment where pupils earn rewards and take part in exciting team events such as Cross Country and Sports Day—much-loved occasions where families cheer them on.

When pupils move into Juniors, they join one of our four main Houses: Lake, Marlborough, Park or School.
The Junior House system offers a wide programme of events and competitions, creative and sporting opportunities for every child, and a nurturing community where teamwork, resilience and leadership thrive. In Senior School, tutor groups align with one of four Houses: Corylus, Ilex, Quercus and Salix. Each House is led by a dedicated Head of House, ensuring consistent pastoral support and strong relationships between pupils, staff and families.

The House Activity Programme
Our House Activity Programme brings the school together through friendly competition and creative expression. Events range from House Music and House Debating to football tournaments and the much-anticipated annual Pancake Race.
Through these shared experiences, pupils strengthen teamwork, creativity, resilience and leadership, skills that last long beyond their school years.

pageCache.pageTitle: Crosfields Celebrates Outstanding GCSE Results - Crosfields School
pageCache.text:
Crosfields Celebrates Outstanding GCSE Results
Crosfields School is celebrating another exceptional set of GCSE results, with pupils achieving impressive outcomes across a wide range of subjects and the school’s value-added performance once again recognised among the top 10% nationally. This year’s results mark an important milestone in the school’s history. As the final cohort to complete their journey at Crosfields before the opening of the School’s Sixth Form in September 2027, pupils leave having helped shape a successful and thriving Senior School community.
The results compare particularly favourably with national outcomes, with the proportion of Grade 9s achieved at Crosfields almost four times the national average and the proportion of Grades 8-9 more than three times the national average. The School’s results have also been rated by ALPs value added as being within the top 10% of schools nationally, recognising the outstanding progress and outcomes achieved by Crosfields pupils throughout their school journey.
Some of the highlights include: 19% of all grades were awarded at Grade 9 39% of grades were awarded at Grades 8-9 90% of grades were awarded at Grades 5-9 97% of grades were awarded at Grades 4-9
Pupils excelled across a number of subjects, including French, where 100% of grades were awarded at 8 or 9. Computer Science saw 89% of grades awarded at 7-9, while 85% of Physics grades and 77% of grades in Chemistry, Spanish, Psychology and Biology were awarded at 7-9.
Several pupils achieved exceptional individual results. Abha was awarded eight Grade 9s, one Grade 8 and an A in Additional Mathematics, while Harveer achieved eight Grade 9s, one Grade 7 and A grades in both HPQ and Additional Mathematics. Evgeniya and Lucy each secured seven Grade 9s and two Grade 8s.
Mrs Caroline Townshend, Head, said: “What makes these results particularly special is that they reflect not only academic excellence, but the individual journeys of our pupils and our commitment to ensuring every child is supported to achieve their very best. This cohort also marks the end of an era. With our new Sixth Form opening in September 2027, they are the final pupils who will leave Crosfields after Year 11. We could not be prouder of their academic success, character, ambition and contribution to school life, all of which have prepared them exceptionally well for the exciting opportunities ahead.”
Mr James Bown, Deputy Head Academic (Seniors), added: “These fantastic achievements extend far beyond examination results. Our pupils have been leaders, role models and active contributors to our community, helping to shape the Senior School we see today. We are delighted to see their hard work and determination rewarded with such excellent outcomes. They leave Crosfields having made a lasting contribution to our community, and we wish every one of them every success as they embark on their next chapter.”
As pupils celebrate their achievements and prepare for the next stage of their educational journeys, the entire Crosfields community congratulates them on their success and wishes them every happiness and success for the future. Families interested in finding out more about Crosfields are warmly invited to attend the School’s Open Morning on Saturday 26 September. Those interested in the new Sixth Form can visit the Sixth Form Information Evening on Tuesday 29 September. To book your place at either event visit: www.crosfields.com/visit
